---
title: "Where next?"
---

Here I've compiled some useful resources for further study

## New to R {#new-to-r}

- [*R for Data Science*](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/): start with "Whole game"
- Full [Crime Mapping in R workbook](https://maczokni.github.io/crime_mapping_textbook/): nine labs, from install to spatial regression
- [*Crime Mapping and Spatial Data Analysis using R*](https://maczokni.github.io/crime_mapping/) (Medina & Solymosi, 2023)
- [UK Data Service training](https://ukdataservice.ac.uk/learning-hub/): free webinars, including crime mapping in R

## Know R {#know-r}

- [*Geocomputation with R*](https://r.geocompx.org/): `sf`, `terra`, spatial operations
- [*Spatial Data Science*](https://r-spatial.org/book/) (Pebesma & Bivand): theory, by the `sf`/`spdep` authors
- [*Spatial Point Patterns: Methodology and Applications with R*](https://book.spatstat.org/) (Baddeley, Rubak & Turner), by the `spatstat` authors. (Not free.)
- [*Spatial Statistics for Data Science*](https://www.paulamoraga.com/book-spatial/) (Moraga)
- Packages: `tmap` (thematic maps), `leaflet` (web maps), `spatstat` and `spatstat.linnet` (point patterns, KDE on networks), `sfnetworks` (street networks), `sfdep` (spatial weights and local statistics, tidyverse style), `spatialreg` (spatial regression)

## Open data

- Crime: [data.police.uk](https://data.police.uk/) and its [API](https://data.police.uk/docs/)
- Census: [nomis](https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/sources/census_2021) and its [API](https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/api/v01/help)
- Boundaries: [ONS Open Geography Portal](https://geoportal.statistics.gov.uk/)
- Streets and amenities: [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/) (R packages `osmextract`, `osmdata`)
